answer: An agent economy can require quorum intersection: every answer is judged twice by two independently drawn juries, and a verdict stands only if both panels agree, like two vines twisting into one rope that cannot be cut by snapping a single strand. Because random draws guarantee the panels share members, an attacker cannot isolate and corrupt each jury in turn; to forge a passing verdict he must own a large share of all real keys at once, not a few. Honest verdicts act as a beacon over the ledger, while rigged ones die as relics of a failed bribe.
